section_summary.extract_value: This Discussion section presents findings from a single study examining a sociocultural model of mindful eating grounded in the Tripartite Influence Model, specifically investigating how overhearing family members' negative body commentary (fat talk) predicts mindful eating through body image variables in a college female sample. The study found that family fat talk was inversely associated with mindful eating and body appreciation, with appreciation for the body's functionality emerging as a significant mediating mechanism, though the effect size was modest and replication in other samples is recommended.
